parsed_answer.content: @SpringBootTest is the heavy-duty integration testing annotation in the Spring ecosystem. It bootstraps the entire ApplicationContext, scanning for @SpringBootApplication, loading all beans, and starting an embedded web server if configured. It is the 'full-stack' approach, ideal for end-to-end testing where you need to verify the interaction between your controllers, services, and repositories. Conversely, @WebMvcTest is a focused slice-test annotation. It only instantiates the web layer—controllers, filters, and interceptors—while mocking the service layer. It is significantly faster because it ignores the database and business logic beans. Finally, @DataJpaTest is designed specifically for the persistence layer. It configures an in-memory database (like H2), scans for @Entity classes, and configures Spring Data JPA repositories. It rolls back transactions by default after every test method, ensuring your database state remains clean and isolated.

items: @SpringBootTest uses @BootstrapWith to load the full context; if your project is large, this can lead to slow build times due to frequent context refreshing.
@WebMvcTest uses MockMvc to simulate HTTP requests without starting a full Servlet container, allowing you to verify @Valid constraints and @ExceptionHandler logic in isolation.
@DataJpaTest automatically enables @Transactional, meaning every test method is wrapped in a transaction that rolls back at the end, preventing side effects between test cases.
Using @DataJpaTest with a real database (via @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)) requires careful management of schema initialization, often necessitating Flyway or Liquibase integration.

parsed_answer.content: The most common production pitfall is 'Context Pollution'. If you use @SpringBootTest across multiple test classes with different @MockBean definitions, Spring will create a new ApplicationContext for each unique configuration. This results in massive memory consumption and slow test suites. Always prefer the slice tests (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest) to keep the context footprint small and test execution fast.
